Hannah M. Pingree

Democratic candidate for Governor, Maine · Open seat

Former Speaker of the Maine House; former director of the Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future

Hannah Pingree is a Democrat from North Haven, Maine. She served eight years in the Maine House, including a term as Speaker, and later led the Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future under Gov. Janet Mills from 2019 to 2025. She won the June 2026 Democratic primary for governor after a ranked-choice runoff.

Where Pingree stands

Housing
Has said she will keep working on Maine's housing crisis, and launched her campaign at a new housing development in Rockland.
Health care
Has said she will work to address Maine's health care shortage.
State budget / bipartisanship
Pledges to bring back a bipartisan approach to the state budget and other hard problems. She points to the two-year budget she negotiated with Republicans while in the Legislature.
Federal policy / tariffs
Has spoken about the effects of the Trump administration's tariffs and budget proposals on Maine, and says Mainers want leaders who will stand up and fight back.

Background

  • Maine House of Representatives, 8 years; Speaker of the House (term ended 2010)
  • Director, Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future, 2019–2025
  • Announced run for governor June 2025
  • Won Democratic nomination for governor, June 2026 (ranked-choice runoff)
  • Resident of North Haven, Maine; daughter of U.S. Rep. Chellie Pingree

Also running for Governor

  • Richard A. Bennett Independent
  • Robert "Bobby" B. Charles Republican
